f4b4bb981e:04747559c4c0f482.title: SKELTCH Business Stationery
f4b4bb981e:04747559c4c0f482.summary: SKELTCH explores the moment when ideas first appear on paper. The identity is built around a dynamic wordmark that behaves like a piece of typed text, constantly shifting, rearranging and forming new compositions. Its unconventional structure reflects the spontaneous nature of creative thinking, where ideas emerge, overlap and take unexpected directions. This approach became the foundation for the packaging design. A vivid orange palette creates an expressive and instantly recognizable visual presence. The wordmark is enhanced with a dimensional 3D finish, turning typography into a tactile element that extends beyond the printed surface. The result is a visual identity that feels energetic, unconventional and unapologetically bold. SKELTCH transforms everyday stationery into an expression of creativity, where even the simplest blank page holds the potential for something new.

f4b4bb981e:6cdbda89b88fd3e4.title: PARASOMA
f4b4bb981e:6cdbda89b88fd3e4.summary: PARASOMA is a research project we're developing at NastPlas on the body an organism would have if it were formed by two biological systems in a stable association. What interests us is the boundary between them: one region densifies because it has to bear tension, another stretches into a membrane, an interface thickens until it becomes a compartment. We start from documented phenomena (lichenization, extracellular matrix, endosymbiosis, differential growth, structural color) and turn them into organizational rules. What comes out of those rules is speculation, and we keep it carefully separate from what has been established. None of these forms exist, but each one should be explainable. There are 21 open series. Each starts from a hypothesis, carries its own risk and its own palette, and we discard a lot. As the research moved forward, the rules started to feel too limited for a still image. So we developed two applications that are part of the project.

f4b4bb981e:6e7fa253f7cf0c90.summary: The Tartu Punch visual identity lets sound shape the visuals: typography crumples as if hit by a kick drum, patterns pulse with the bass, and vibrations tear backgrounds apart. Rooted in the physical sensation of music?the kind of bass felt through the whole body?the graphic language translates sound into distortion, rhythm, and contrast. This approach carries across posters, merchandise, and stage screens, bringing the same energy to every format. Bold colour combinations and shifting patterns keep the identity in motion, even in print, while distorted letterforms give it a distinctive voice. Music becomes a visible presence, felt before it's even heard.

f4b4bb981e:4f9a5f711cf956c2.title: Good Genes ? Zetland
f4b4bb981e:4f9a5f711cf956c2.summary: A series of illustrations for Good Genes, an investigative podcast by the Danish outlet Zetland. A journalist follows a Dane in the US who screens wealthy couples' embryos for disease risk, height and IQ ? a trail that leads to a castle in East Germany, stolen IQ data from the Danish military, and an online race-theory network. Art direction: Nina Gantriis Zetland, 2026

f4b4bb981e:0feb901cfb361041.title: IT WAS ALL A DREAM
f4b4bb981e:0feb901cfb361041.summary: This artistic project series delves into the exploration of distinct worlds encountered during my recent dreams, expanding upon my imaginative realm and imbuing them with significance through the act of drawing and rendering them tangible in the physical world. This project serves as a testament to the potency of human imagination, emotions, and the fact that even digital abstract artworks acquire profound meaning when crafted from the ground up by a human mind. This is because they inevitably reveal a fragmentary and intimate aspect of my being, simultaneously exhibiting simplicity and intricacy.

f4b4bb981e:53d9d2e3568bee34.title: KEMONO - ?
f4b4bb981e:53d9d2e3568bee34.summary: ?/KEMONO is a personal illustration series inspired by ancient Japanese culture, samurai traditions, and the charm of animal characters. The series reimagines animals such as turtles, rabbits, and orangutan as ancient warriors, each with their own personality, weapons, and distinctive armor. By combining animal characteristics with traditional Japanese warrior aesthetics, KEMONO creates a world where different creatures share the same spirit of courage, honor, and adventure.

f4b4bb981e:d88daee2c511184a.title: Pleto Iconography
f4b4bb981e:d88daee2c511184a.summary: A flexible iconography system designed for Pleto, combining geometric simplicity, visual clarity, and adaptable stroke weights to create a distinctive visual language.

f4b4bb981e:bd447aa6d99768d0.title: Various Illustration. People.
f4b4bb981e:bd447aa6d99768d0.summary: A collection of illustrations exploring the limits of vector illustration and shaping a unique visual style. Focusing on people, fashion and daily life.

f4b4bb981e:12e6423724e1f747.title: Compilation 37
f4b4bb981e:12e6423724e1f747.summary: A new selection of geometric and psychedelic illustrations by YoAz. Bold color relationships, intricate linework and carefully balanced compositions turn familiar shapes into vivid graphic worlds. This collection reflects an ongoing exploration of symmetry, rhythm and visual storytelling through contemporary illustration.

f4b4bb981e:27940173d155d016.title: Cash & Carry
f4b4bb981e:27940173d155d016.summary: A series of illustrated typographic artworks inspired by South Africa's hand-painted shop signage. Drawing on these everyday visuals, the project explores custom lettering through a playful, contemporary lens.

f4b4bb981e:13316ca9cf114d84.title: HOFF Collaboration
f4b4bb981e:13316ca9cf114d84.summary: A capsule collection with HOFF, the sneaker brand from Elche, Spain. I brought my visual language onto their shoes: simple geometric shapes, contrasting colors and a bit of sarcasm. The project covered the sneakers, a T-shirt and a custom box for the limited edition. My favorite detail is hidden inside: the insole carries the first sketch of the collection, the rough drawing where the whole design started.

f4b4bb981e:1b390e3fe9d04fd2.title: Imagination Day 12
f4b4bb981e:1b390e3fe9d04fd2.summary: Imagination Day is a true celebration of creativity ? an event that brings together visionaries, makers, and speakers from around the world. With each edition, its ambition and momentum continued to grow, but the visual identity could no longer keep up with the pace of the industry. That's why we set out to create an entirely new visual language: bold, flexible, and expansive enough to capture the diversity of today's creative landscape. The result is a complete rebrand, a set of fresh visual assets, and a new website that give Imagination Day the energy to move confidently into the years ahead.

f4b4bb981e:54de2ed297e0f28e.title: TONANA
f4b4bb981e:54de2ed297e0f28e.summary: Coatlicue-Tonantzin is the mother goddess of nature, death, and the mother of the gods in the Mesoamerican worldview, particularly within the Mexica tradition. As the archetypal great mother, she embodies the feminine principle that gives life within nature. For this project we worked with interior and furniture designer Andrés Gutiérrez, who?guided by a vivid color palette inspired by Mesoamerican cosmology?selected marbles, volcanic stones, and textured materials for building a bar inspired by the mother goddess of the Mexica pantheon. Within that chromatic range and the primordial creation myth, we developed a graphic identity based on these concepts and on the furniture and interior design created by Andrés Gutiérrez, drawing on elements such as the serpent, femininity, and maternity, as well as Mexican aesthetics associated with the goddess Coatlicue-Tonantzin. To produce the graphic pieces?stationery, the menu, digital applications, etc.?we referenced Mesoamerican codices,.

f4b4bb981e:0c6acecbb865747b.title: GEOTHERMAL LAYERS ? Iceland
f4b4bb981e:0c6acecbb865747b.summary: Abstract aerial studies of Icelandic geothermal terrain, where pale blue water, mineral crusts and altered clay form delicate channels, cracks and layered textures across the volcanic ground.

a4977d3fa4:a0519f3c7123ece2.title: Vincent Tsang Brings Quiet Luxury to the Fairway With PIERRE
a4977d3fa4:a0519f3c7123ece2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a0519f3c7123ece2.summary: Summary Dime artistic director Vincent Tsang serves as artistic director for PIERRE, a new golf-inspired luxury apparel labelDesigned in Montréal and manufactured in Japan, the brand crafts garments from silk and premium materials without loud logosThe official website is now live with all products available to purchase via pierre.golf PIERRE is a newly introduced luxury apparel label with Dime artistic director Vincent Tsang serving as its artistic director, built on the core belief that true luxury is felt before it is seen. Designed in Montréal and meticulously manufactured in Japan, the newly minted golf lifestyle and apparel brand blends thoughtful Montréal design with the precision and craftsmanship of Japanese manufacturing to establish an understated wardrobe for those who value quality over spectacle.Drawing direct inspiration from golf’s enduring relationship with nature, PIERRE celebrates patience, presence, and the beauty of moving at a slower pace. Rather than chasing fleeting trends or relying on loud logos, the imprint creates garments that honor both the natural rhythm of the game and the landscapes it inhabits. Through this measured approach, each piece is conceived to embody quiet confidence, timeless style, and lasting comfort.Materiality and tailoring sit at the center of the label’s creative direction. Placing uncompromising fabric and considered fit at the forefront of every garment, PIERRE crafts its pieces from a refined mix of silk and other premium materials. Engineered to move effortlessly between the golf course and everyday life, the resulting wardrobe offers versatile, tactile staples defined by subtle luxury and enduring wearability.The official PIERRE website is now live online. a4977d3fa4:2b1497fe7b8e66ad.title: Mercedes-Benz Unveils Holographic Tech to Turn Windshields Into Screens
a4977d3fa4:2b1497fe7b8e66ad.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2b1497fe7b8e66ad.summary: Summary Mercedes-Benz has announced Holo Display technology that turns a vehicle windshield into a transparent screenUsing a dashboard projector and laminated holographic film the system displays sunlight-readable visuals tailored separately to driver and passenger viewing anglesThe automaker is also developing Intelligent Display in Glass to project safety symbols and traffic warnings through side and rear windows German luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz has announced its new Holo Display and Intelligent Display in Glass technologies, expanding automotive screens directly onto vehicle windows. Building upon the dashboard-spanning Hyperscreen introduced earlier this decade, both next-generation display systems remain virtually invisible to the naked eye when not actively in use.Currently termed the Holo Display, the windshield system pairs a dashboard-integrated projector with a specialized transparent film laminated onto the interior glass. Utilizing holographic optical elements to reflect light wavelengths emitted by the projector, the setup produces imagery strong enough to remain legible even in bright sunlight, improving upon current-generation head-up displays. Engineered to prevent distraction, the display restricts viewing angles so drivers and passengers see isolated visuals—delivering navigation and vehicle data to the driver while offering passengers video calls, journey points of interest, and films.Alongside the windshield projection setup, Mercedes-Benz is developing Intelligent Display in Glass for a vehicle's side and rear windows. Integrating subtle LED display elements directly into the glass panels, the system allows vehicles to communicate externally with their surroundings by projecting warning signs, safety symbols, and traffic-related alerts only when needed. a4977d3fa4:0fedc76692143cf3.title: The Nike Zoom Vomero 5 Vapor Pro “Black/Metallic Silver” Takes the Lifestyle Icon to the Gridiron
a4977d3fa4:0fedc76692143cf3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)

The design holds onto enough of the original’s layered upper to stay instantly recognizable, then swaps the chunky running sole for a studded plate and a collar built for the gridiron.The Vomero 5 first arrived in the late 2000s as a technical running shoe before its recent revival turned it into a fixture of the Y2K-inspired lifestyle wave. That history is part of what makes this conversion notable, as Nike is applying the Vapor name, long attached to its speed-focused football cleats, to a model better known for coffee runs than cuts and sprints.Up top, the black mesh base anchors a build that keeps the Vomero 5’s DNA intact. Metallic silver overlays climb from the toe box through the lacing zone, while oversized silver Swooshes sweep across both the medial and lateral sides. The model’s familiar ribbed panels still sit below each Swoosh, gray striping fills in around the midfoot, and a faint triangle print wraps the heel for a subtle hit of texture.The most visible departure from the runner sits at the ankle. A black knit collar extends upward to hug the lower leg, finished with pull tabs at the front and rear for easier entry, plus a Nike Vapor tag placed just above the laces to mark the cleat’s performance lineage. White laces come installed, though product imagery also shows swap-in pairs in black, red and bright green for players looking to match team colors.Underfoot, a crisp white sole runs the full length of the shoe, extending through the molded studs for a clean contrast against the dark upper. a4977d3fa4:ccb763eb42ffc49c.title: Globe-Trotter and YOSHIROTTEN Split a “SUPERNOVA” Across Three Suitcases
a4977d3fa4:ccb763eb42ffc49c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ccb763eb42ffc49c.summary: Summary Globe-Trotter and YOSHIROTTEN have built a three-piece suitcase set that forms one continuous artwork when the cases stand side by sideThe graphics draw from YOSHIROTTEN’s “SUPERNOVA” work, layering nebula blues, oranges, pinks and greens over the brand’s signature black fiberboardThe release commemorates the artist’s 'BEYOND EARTH' exhibition, currently on view at TOKYO NODE in Tokyo’s Toranomon Hills Globe-Trotter has teamed up with Tokyo-based artist YOSHIROTTEN on the “SUPERNOVA” suitcase set, a limited trio of hard-shell cases that only reveals its full image when all three pieces are lined up together. Created to mark YOSHIROTTEN’s BEYOND EARTH exhibition, the project translates his large-scale cosmic imagery onto a functional travel object, turning a matching luggage set into a single, modular canvas.Each case starts from Globe-Trotter’s defining material, a black vulcanized fiberboard shell that serves as the dark backdrop for YOSHIROTTEN’s palette. Over that base, the artist stacks bands of blue, orange, pink and green meant to evoke drifting nebulae and distant horizon lines, pulling directly from “SUPERNOVA,” his piece exploring the dramatic life cycles of stars. Because the composition runs continuously across all three shells, no single suitcase tells the whole story, which is why the cases are sold strictly as a set rather than individually.The hardware details lean into longevity. Handles are cut from natural leather that gradually darkens into a rich amber tone with use, so every set will develop its own patina depending on how often it travels. Opening any of the cases reveals YOSHIROTTEN’s handwritten signature on the interior, marking each piece as an authenticated part of the edition.In terms of sizing, every suitcase measures 58cm wide, 42cm tall and 21cm deep, offering 34L of capacity, putting all three cases on identical footprints so the artwork aligns cleanly when displayed. a4977d3fa4:39af0223e1f68d58.title: Wicker, Coachwork and Sapphires Take Center Stage at Sotheby’s ‘The Human Touch’
a4977d3fa4:39af0223e1f68d58.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:39af0223e1f68d58.summary: Summary Sotheby’s hosts The Human Touch from November 23 – 28, a special exhibition celebrating luxury handcraftsmanship.Highlights include a wicker Hermès Mini Kelly Picnic and Morgan’s Midsummer Coupé.Creations by Charles Frodsham and Moussaieff Jewellers spotlight human artistry. This month, Sotheby’s is presenting The Human Touch, a special exhibition spotlighting the enduring value of handcraftsmanship across the global luxury ecosystem. Bringing together a curated mix of rare automobiles, watches, jewelry and collectibles, the showcase celebrates the human ingenuity and technical mastery behind some of the most sought-after creations on the market in an era increasingly shaped by automation.Leading the presentation is the coveted Hermès Mini Kelly Picnic, a standout example of artisanal savoir-faire that pairs a hand-woven natural wicker body with smooth pale blue-gray leather across its top flap, handle, and signature sangles, finished with silver-tone turn-lock hardware.Anchoring the exhibition’s automotive narrative is British marque Morgan Motor Company, celebrated for over a century of bespoke coachbuilding that blends traditional hand-built techniques with contemporary engineering. Headlining its presence is the one-of-a-kind Morgan Midsummer Coupé “The Artists’ Proof,” showcasing sweeping sculpted fenders, a classic vertical-slat grille, and a sleek enclosed cabin finished in a deep, dark metallic hue.Horological and high-jewelry craftsmanship are equally represented through the Charles Frodsham Double Impulse Chronometer “Hidden Seconds” - distinguished by its crisp white dial, dark blue Arabic numerals, blued-steel hands, and contrast-stitched black leather strap - and an intricate Y-drop necklace from Moussaieff Jewellers that weaves royal blue, purple and pink sapphires into diamond-set ribbons.As James Marks, Sotheby’s SVP and Global Head of Private Sales & Retail, Watches, noted, while the featured objects span vastly different disciplines,…

a4977d3fa4:d11780515c284de4.title: Jamie Pearl on the Art of Photographing Fame
a4977d3fa4:d11780515c284de4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d11780515c284de4.summary: Summary Jamie Pearl reflects on capturing candid moments with Doechii, Dennis Rodman, Nina Dobrev and other cultural figures.From spontaneous celebrity portraits to experimental editorial work, the photographer shares a creative approach shaped by energy, instinct and authenticity. Some of the most memorable celebrity photographs happen when no one's quite ready for the camera. A cigarette break outside a Fashion Week dinner, a fleeting moment in the backseat of a car, or the final touches before a red carpet appearance can reveal more personality than a carefully staged portrait. For New York-based photographer Jamie Pearl, those in-between moments have become the foundation of a practice rooted in spontaneity and human connection.After discovering black-and-white film photography in high school, Jamie eventually found a footing in New York's fashion and entertainment circles, capturing everyone from Dennis Rodman and Doechii to Keke Palmer and Nina Dobrev. While the fast-paced world of celebrity events has sharpened an instinct for the unexpected, a growing interest in editorial photography has opened up new possibilities for creative experimentation. We caught up with Jamie to discuss memorable encounters, the art of thinking on your feet, and why the best images often happen when you least expect them."In the words of one of my favorite photographers, Tyrell Hampton, it’s all about energy."How did you first get into photography, and when did you start shooting celebrities?I first got into photography about 13 years ago, when I was a 15-year-old high school student. I attended an arts-focused high school, which I credit with so much of my creative development. I always knew I was an artist, but when my drawings weren’t turning out quite how I envisioned them in my head, and I realized I didn’t exactly have a knack for playing the piano, I knew I needed to do some exploring to find my medium. Luckily, going to a high school that offered such a wide range of art…

a4977d3fa4:f41aa86632f927b5.summary: Summary Artist Barry McGee has unveiled a new "solo" exhibition at Jeffrey Deitch's Los Angeles outpost, titled 'Another Round'The exhibition, running through January 30, 2027, features over 200 paintings, sculptures, and photographs by McGee alongside hundreds of works from friends and collaborators, including a mini fabrication of '99CENTS,' his knockout anti-art fair presentation earlier this year After he opened a knockout 99CENT in February, artist Barry McGee is back in Los Angeles for Another Round, his new exhibition at Jeffrey Deitch's Santa Monica Boulevard space. The graffiti writer-turned contemporary art star gathers over 200 paintings, sculptures, and photographs to envelope the space. It's his first show with Deitch in 20 years, and in the spirit of the Frieze anti-fair, was made possible with a little help from his friends.While billed as such, the show is less of a “solo” than a snapshot of McGee's place in the art world: his curatorial style and unique place in high-low culture. “In this day and age, a solo anything seems ridiculous,” he recently told The Los Angeles Times. “The ego of the artist is a tricky thing.”Highlights include a bulbous hang of prints and photographs oozing from the walls of the main gallery and kaleidoscopic tiled works peppered throughout. Crowded between them are works by the likes of CHITO, Chris Lux, Todd James, Tom Franco, C. R. Stecky III, and more, like a painted bench by Alfonzo Gonzalez Jr. and KATSU's incognito tagger, a robotic arm spraying from the inside of a bush.Another Round also includes two mock storefronts — galleries within the gallery — created with fellow artist Alexis Ross. One sees a condensed refabrication of the original 99-cent store, linoleum floor, pegboard shelving, and all, spilling with pieces from the show. The other is a bookshop run by Heavy Manners Library's Matthew James-Wilson, which carries zines, books, T-shirts, and McGee's favorite granola.For the exhibition text, Deitch, the…

a4977d3fa4:55f7e7d614c137cf.title: Culture Over Couture: Why Luxury is Doubling Down on Streetwear
a4977d3fa4:55f7e7d614c137cf.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:55f7e7d614c137cf.summary: To understand why European luxury fashion houses are frantically reverting to "buzzy" logos, viral collaborations, and streetwear architects, we have to look past the runway and into the balance sheets. The recent game of creative director musical chairs, which saw Martine Rose appointed as Balenciaga's new creative director following Pierpaolo Piccioli's brief 16 months stint, is not just a shift in aesthetic taste—it is a defensive maneuver against a severe macroeconomic reality.People are simply not buying luxury like they used to. In 2026 alone, Europe’s top luxury conglomerates had roughly $350 billion USD wiped from their market value amid a prolonged spending slowdown, heavily driven by a pullback in the Chinese market and the evaporation of aspirational shoppers. When consumption power plummets, quiet luxury doesn't pay the bills; brands need massive cultural noise to stimulate a stagnant market.The Attention Economy: Instant Cool Over Quiet HeritageThis economic reality is compounded by a fundamental shift in how technology has rewired our consumption behavior. With infinite information at our fingertips, consumer attention spans have been severely fractured by the algorithmic churn of TikTok and Instagram. In this hyper-connected ecosystem, trends live and die at breakneck speeds, and the traditional six-month fashion calendar feels painfully slow to a consumer conditioned by the feed. Today's audience is perpetually chasing "the cool"—and they demand it immediately.Consequently, traditional brand "heritage" is losing its standalone currency. Heritage demands patience; it requires the consumer to appreciate the slow, quiet romance of archival history and artisanal craft. But in a digital landscape dominated by visual noise, quiet gets scrolled past. "Instant cool"—a subversive logo flip, an unexpected sneaker drop, or a viral celebrity co-sign—registers in a microsecond. To keep a chronically bored, easily distracted audience interested, luxury brands…

a4977d3fa4:61101cab885ec511.title: Gentle Monster Brings Its Intelligent Eyewear Collection to NYC Ahead of Its December Launch
a4977d3fa4:61101cab885ec511.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:61101cab885ec511.summary: Summary Gentle Monster previews its 16-piece Intelligent Eyewear Collection in New York.Co-engineered with Google and Samsung, the 40-gram frames integrate Gemini AI and a 12MP camera.Priced from $449 USD, the line launches December 10. Gentle Monster is unveiling its full Intelligent Eyewear Collection for the first time at a public preview in New York City, running from November 13 - 23, 2026, at 23 Wall Street.Open to visitors via online registration, the exhibition marks the public’s first opportunity to experience the Seoul-based eyewear house’s debut line of wearable technology in person. Rather than presenting the frames as conventional consumer electronics, Gentle Monster is introducing the 16-piece optical and sunglass lineup through an immersive, gallery-style showcase that reflects the label’s reputation for avant-garde retail installations and experimental aesthetics.Developed through a three-way partnership with Google and Samsung, the lineup covers six frames, two optical styles and four sunglasses, offered in 16 combinations of colorways and lenses. a4977d3fa4:3d95ea0791a99c8f.title: doublet Turns Your Most Used Emojis Into a Bag for FW26
a4977d3fa4:3d95ea0791a99c8f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3d95ea0791a99c8f.summary: Summary doublet’s FW26 "EMOJI LEATHER BAG" features 3D cowhide emoji expressions.The design physicalizes unseen human emotions to lighten emotional weight.It releases November 9 for approx. $860 USD at select retailers. Masayuki Ino’s doublet has always thrived on humor and subversion, turning the mundane into the unexpected. For its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, the brand taps into everyday emojis and turns them into something you can wear with the EMOJI LEATHER BAG.The playful design stems from a longstanding adage: bags that look like faces sell well. doublet took the saying literally, utilizing intricate leather patching and precise stitching to recreate three emoji expressions in three dimensions across the front of the bags. The available expressions include the crying-laughing face, the pleading face, and the green vomiting face.Crafted from soft cowhide leather, the tote balances its loud exterior with practical, everyday utility. Equipped with a detachable shoulder strap, allowing the wearer to effortlessly switch between hand-carry and crossbody styling.Beyond its immediate visual punchline, the design carries a deeper meaning. doublet finds that human emotions are inherently invisible. The brand wants to explore how, by boldly wearing these unseen feelings as a physical object, the wearer could reduce the emotional weight they carry and make them feel lighter.Available in Camel and Black, the doublet EMOJI LEATHER BAG releases on November 9, available for ¥137,500 JPY (approx. $860 USD) at doublet’s online store, and select retailers in Japan. a4977d3fa4:004ef2a8120ca4e4.title: Toyota Is Finally Bringing a Kei Truck to America, but It Tops Out at 25 MPH
a4977d3fa4:004ef2a8120ca4e4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:004ef2a8120ca4e4.summary: Summary Toyota is reviving the Scion brand to launch the miniature KEI-01 pickup truck in the United States in late 2027Measuring just over 11 feet long with a 660cc engine and four-wheel drive, the right-hand-drive truck tops out at 25 mph under federal low-speed vehicle rulesAssembled in Indiana, the KEI-01 will initially launch through a limited pilot program for fleet customers via selected dealers Toyota is bringing Japan’s miniature pickup culture stateside with the new KEI-01, a compact utility truck launching under the revived Scion brand in the second half of 2027. Reintroduced a decade after its discontinuation around the “freedom to explore mobility in new ways,” Scion will debut the pint-sized truck as a practical alternative to full-size American pickups.Measuring just over 11 feet long and under five feet wide, the right-hand-drive KEI-01 is powered by a 660cc three-cylinder gasoline engine paired with an automatic transmission and selectable four-wheel drive. Despite its compact footprint, the truck hauls up to 600 pounds in a three-way fold-down cargo bed and can tow small trailers. Inside the enclosed extended cabin, drivers get heating, air conditioning, sliding and reclining seats, and rear storage for tools. To meet federal low-speed vehicle safety regulations, however, the truck tops out at 25 mph—restricting it in many states to roads with speed limits of 35 mph or less.Backed by a $34 million USD investment creating roughly 50 jobs, assembly will begin at Toyota’s Indiana factory in the second half of 2027.The Scion KEI-01 drops in late 2027 through a limited fleet pilot program via selected dealers for businesses, farms, and universities, with broader retail sales and pricing to be announced later Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:9aa36ba1b40259a1.title: Theaster Gates Recasts Tar, Clay and Gym Floors for His Hong Kong Exhibition ‘Surrogate’
a4977d3fa4:9aa36ba1b40259a1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9aa36ba1b40259a1.summary: Summary Theaster Gates revisits his signature motifs in ‘Surrogate,’ transferring them onto new materials or setting them in fresh compositionsThe show includes fire-hose imprints in clay, reclaimed gymnasium flooring, a clay “handbag” and a trio of new Tar PaintingsThe exhibition explores how art can stand in for something absent, whether a family bond, a community or a history that has been overlooked Theaster Gates brings Surrogate, an exhibition of new works, to Gagosian Hong Kong from November 19. The show finds the Chicago-based artist mining his own visual language, lifting elements from earlier series and reworking them through different materials and arrangements. Each piece is built on the idea that an artwork can act on behalf of something that isn’t there, a thread that has run through Gates’ practice for more than a decade.Fire hoses offer the clearest example of that material shift. Gates has used decommissioned hoses since 2011 in his Civil Tapestries, flat, striped compositions that call up the hoses turned on civil rights protesters. For Surrogate, he presses those same hoses into slabs of clay, so the ridged texture once read as fabric and paint now sits in fired ceramic surfaces.A similar reworking happens with his “gym floor” pieces, a series he started in 2014 using varnished planks salvaged from school gymnasiums. Rather than leaving the court lines in their original layout, Gates has reorganized the painted markings into graphic bands. The new geometry echoes a set of paintings he made in the late 2010s, which drew on the data visualizations of Black life that sociologist W. E. B. Du Bois and his students produced in 1900.The exhibition’s clay “handbag” moves the conversation from flat surfaces to form. A handbag is useful and also signals taste and identity, and Gates uses it to extend his long-running interest in vessels, from ceramic pots to buildings, as objects that hold and protect what is placed inside them. The piece also connects to…

a4977d3fa4:aebc9d64ce2ac36e.title: ‘GTA VII’ Outside America? Rockstar Won’t Rule It Out
a4977d3fa4:aebc9d64ce2ac36e.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:aebc9d64ce2ac36e.summary: Summary Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson has declined to rule out a ‘Grand Theft Auto’ game set outside the US, though he stopped short of confirming any plansThe comments land as ‘GTA VI’ prepares to launch with what is described as the series’ most detailed recreation of America to dateRockstar has weighed overseas settings before, with a shelved ‘GTA: Tokyo’ concept and pitches spanning Rio de Janeiro, Moscow, Istanbul, London and Paris Grand Theft Auto may not be bound to American soil forever, with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson signaling that an international setting remains possible for the franchise. Speaking with The Guardian ahead of GTA VI’s launch, Nelson was asked whether Rockstar could picture a mainline entry outside the US. His answer left room for it, though he did not reference a specific sequel or commit to any destination.Nelson’s full response was brief and carefully balanced. “Never say never, but there’s still so much to do in America,” he told The Guardian. The line keeps the series’ home turf firmly in focus while acknowledging that a departure is not off limits. Any talk of a GTA VII setting remains speculation, since Rockstar has yet to formally announce a follow-up.The scale of what Rockstar builds helps explain the caution. GTA VI returns players to Vice City, the studio’s fictional stand-in for Miami, and expands outward into the surrounding state of Leonida. The game has spent more than a decade in development and is billed as the franchise’s most detailed take on America yet, which sets an enormous bar for any city Rockstar might attempt next. Recreating a foreign capital at that fidelity would mean rebuilding street-level cultural knowledge, signage, traffic patterns and local character from scratch rather than iterating on familiar ground. Leonida itself is modeled on Florida.That familiar ground has defined the series for decades. Liberty City, Los Santos and Vice City have rotated through the franchise as…

a4977d3fa4:562cb08847cbbd00.summary: Summary Jean-Michel Basquiat sets out to recover the person behind one of the art world’s most mythologized names, using family recollections that have never been toldPreviously unseen works and rare archival imagery form the visual backbone of the documentaryThe film earned Best Editing in a Documentary Feature at the 2026 Tribeca Festival, where it held its world premiere Jean-Michel Basquiat, the new documentary from directors Quinn Whitney Wilson and Viridiana Lieberman, premieres globally on Netflix on December 11 following an award-winning world premiere at the 2026 Tribeca Festival. Rather than retracing the familiar arc of the artist’s meteoric rise, the film sets out to recover what decades of myth-making have obscured. Its goal is to strip back the legend and arrive at Jean-Michel himself.The documentary is built on three kinds of material, and the first is the most personal. Untold memories from Basquiat’s own family sit at the center of the film, offering an inside perspective that most retellings of his life have had to do without. That family presence extends behind the camera as well, with Lisane Basquiat and Jeanine Heriveaux credited among the executive producers. The two are the artist’s younger sisters.Layered against those accounts are works by Basquiat that have never been shown before, alongside rare archival imagery. Together they give the film a visual record that goes beyond the paintings audiences already know. For a figure whose output has been endlessly reproduced, the promise of unseen material is the documentary’s sharpest selling point.Shaping that much archive into a coherent portrait is an editing challenge, and the film’s handling of it has already been recognized. At its Tribeca world premiere, Jean-Michel Basquiat took home the award for Best Editing in a Documentary Feature, a nod to how the filmmakers stitched family testimony, artwork and historical footage into a single narrative.Wilson and Lieberman direct, and Wilson also…

The proposed deal is structured as an absorption, with the aerospace company swallowing the automaker while negotiations determine exactly how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors will receive. Following its June IPO, SpaceX is currently valued at over $1.9 trillion USD, while Tesla commands an approximate $1.5 trillion USD valuation. Combining the two entities would mark the largest corporate merger in history, entirely dwarfing the previous record set by Vodafone’s $183 billion USD takeover of Mannesmann in 2000. After the publication of the report, Tesla’s stock price immediately increased by as much as 1.9%, though neither SpaceX nor Tesla provided a comment regarding the ongoing negotiations.The mechanics of the deal hinge heavily on price and control terms. Elon Musk previously confirmed in October that both companies' boards had established special committees to explore the merger, but the boardroom overlap is already deeply established. Ira Ehrenpreis, who currently chairs Tesla's compensation and governance committees, has served on the SpaceX board since February. Tesla is scheduled to hold its annual shareholder meeting on December 3, where the exact directors required to approve the monumental deal are up for re-election. a4977d3fa4:d8c7a6df58ace5e9.summary: Summary Aston Martin has partnered with Disney and Lucasfilm to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Star Wars franchiseThe automaker filed a trademark in March 2024 for Venator, a name tied to the Republic's Star DestroyersThe unconventional collaboration aims to generate publicity amid an ongoing cash crunch and recent debt financing In a major pop-culture pivot, Aston Martin partnered with Disney and Lucasfilm to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Star Wars franchise. Celebrations will span the next year through a series of dedicated activations and collaborations. Finbar McFall, global marketing director for Aston Martin, oversees the promotional campaign that links British ultra-luxury craftsmanship with cinematic storytelling.This effort represents an unconventional marketing move for the automaker, which traditionally aligns with the James Bond film series. No Aston Martin vehicle has ever appeared in a Star Wars film. Despite the lack of past on-screen integration, a key piece of cinematic synergy recently surfaced in the brand's legal paperwork.In March 2024, Aston Martin filed to trademark the Venator name. That specific title carries weight in the sci-fi universe as the name of the Republic's Venator-class Star Destroyers in the 2005 film Revenge of the Sith. The ships also appeared regularly in The Clone Wars animated series, cementing their place in franchise lore.Details regarding the 50th anniversary program for Star Wars will arrive in early 2027. The high-profile push comes during a critical financial period for the company. In July 2026, Aston Martin secured roughly $735 million USD in new debt financing to address an ongoing cash crunch. Company executives stated the funding will help deliver upcoming product plans. Securing high-visibility corporate partnerships allows struggling luxury brands to maintain public interest while navigating heavy debt loads and product rollouts. a4977d3fa4:c403b0c9eabe481c.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Reaches $1 Billion USD in Pre-Order Sales Ahead of Release
a4977d3fa4:c403b0c9eabe481c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:c403b0c9eabe481c.summary: Summary Grand Theft Auto VI has reached $1 billion in sales eight days ahead of its November 19 release according to Sensor TowerThe milestone represents an estimated 10.31 million pre-order units sold with PlayStation accounting for 75% and Xbox taking 25%Outpacing its 2013 predecessor in pre-orders the title is projected to break Grand Theft Auto V's 24-hour entertainment revenue record Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two have achieved a massive commercial milestone with Grand Theft Auto VI, which has surpassed $1 billion USD in sales eight days ahead of its official launch. According to market research firm Sensor Tower, the title reached the benchmark through an estimated 10.31 million pre-order units sold, with PlayStation accounting for 75% of sales and Xbox representing 25%.The pre-order surge already outpaces Grand Theft Auto V, which logged 7 million pre-orders ahead of its 2013 debut before reaching 11 million units at launch and 16 million by the end of its first week. While Take-Two has not disclosed official figures, CEO Strauss Zelnick noted during an earnings call that pre-orders are tracking well above initial expectations, helping lift Take-Two shares over 3% to $231.83 USD. Across its lifetime, GTA V has sold roughly 235 million copies, bringing total franchise sales to nearly 480 million units.Arriving after two production delays—moving from fall 2025 to May 2026 before landing on November 19—the release has weathered August gameplay leaks tied to Rockstar’s decision to forego physical discs. Industry analysts project Grand Theft Auto VI to shatter GTA V’s 24-hour entertainment revenue record of $815.7 million USD. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:866ee5b5ed727dac.title: Zenith Heads West for Its Second G.F.J. Double Signed Collaboration
a4977d3fa4:866ee5b5ed727dac.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:866ee5b5ed727dac.summary: Summary Zenith taps J.N. Shapiro for the second G.F.J. Calibre 135 Double Signed edition.A California-made guilloché dial features barleycorn, basketweave and Infinity Weave patterns/Damaskeened bridges bring American flair to the Swiss movement. Zenith is continuing its Double Signed program, a series that revives the golden-era tradition of watches bearing two makers' names. After the first edition with Tokyo's Naoya Hida & Co., the Le Locle Manufacture has teamed up with American independent J.N. Shapiro for the second edition.Both releases are built on the G.F.J., named after Zenith founder Georges Favre-Jacot and designed as the modern home of the Calibre 135, the most decorated observatory chronometer movement in history. Joshua Shapiro started his brand in a home workshop in 2018 making guilloché dials, and it has since grown to produce its own Caliber 26 movement and the Resurgence watch. "The Calibre 135 is one of the holy grails of watchmaking. To get to beautify such a functionally historic calibre has been really exciting," Shapiro said in the release.The dial of the Zenith G.F.J. Calibre 135 Double Signed With J.N. Shapiro was made entirely at Shapiro's California workshop. Its silver base carries three hand-cut guilloché patterns, made on rose-engine and straight-line machines: barleycorn around the outer ring, basketweave in the center, and Shapiro's signature Infinity Weave on the small seconds subdial. Applied 18k rose gold rings, hour markers and nameplates frame the textures, including a "Zenith | J.N. Shapiro" double signature and the G.F.J. initials.Unlike the Naoya Hida edition, which focused on the dial and hands, this collaboration extends to the movement. The bridges of the hand-wound Calibre 135 are decorated with damaskeening, a mix of Côtes de Genève stripes and guilloché patterns closely associated with antique American pocket watches, bringing an American touch to a Swiss movement.Beneath the decoration, the re-engineered Calibre 135…

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company's transformation as a graphics-chip maker into a major supplier of processors powering today's AI needs. Capping a swift fall for one of the central figures in the artificial intelligence boom, the departure follows a multi-hour board meeting on Wednesday convened to weigh Huang’s fate amid revelations of two extramarital affairs.According to the reports, Huang admitted to an extramarital relationship with a woman whom U.S. intelligence agencies concluded was spying for China. Separately, five anonymous former Nvidia employees revealed that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care—an executive who reported directly to him, running counter to the company’s code of conduct barring personal relationships that create workplace conflicts of interest.Although Huang fought to retain his position at the company he founded, an interim plan for Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to take over Nvidia was already well underway. Unwinding Huang’s unconventional, flat management structure—which bypassed traditional organizational charts in favor of more than 60 direct reports, project-focused meetings across all levels, and thousands of daily emails—could complicate a leadership transition. a4977d3fa4:5901aa140d9e90db.title: RIMOWA and Maison Margiela Unveil Limited-Edition Bianchetto Travel Collection
a4977d3fa4:5901aa140d9e90db.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5901aa140d9e90db.summary: Summary RIMOWA and Maison Margiela have unveiled a limited-edition travel set featuring the Classic Cabin suitcase and 5AC XL bagBoth pieces are finished with hand-painted Bianchetto white paint that cracks and forms a unique patina with wearThe collaborative collection releases on November 19 at select stores and online priced at €3200 and €3600 German luggage purveyor RIMOWA and French luxury fashion house Maison Margiela have partnered on a limited-edition travel collection, introducing a collaborative Classic Cabin suitcase and 5AC XL bag. Designed to gradually crack, chip, and flake with regular travel, the treatment develops an evolving patina alongside RIMOWA's aviation-inspired grooved surface. The Classic Cabin, manufactured at RIMOWA's Cologne factory, incorporates an inside-out white lining with visible stitching and overlocked edges, an aluminum logo badge secured with four white stitches, a stage-free telescopic handle, TSA-approved locks, and a Multiwheel system.Mirroring the luggage, the 5AC XL bag translates RIMOWA's signature grooves directly into leather using a seamless high-frequency technique. Built with an exposed lining, a leather crossbody strap, and removable loops that attach atop the suitcase's handle, the bag aligns with the suitcase grooves into a unified set. A bespoke leather tag combining RIMOWA’s address tag and Margiela's key bell finishes both pieces.The RIMOWA x Maison Margiela Classic Cabin and 5AC XL Bag will be available starting November 19, 2026, at RIMOWA and Maison Margiela. a4977d3fa4:d8d73dfdeaea39bb.title: 'Avengers Endgame: Encore' Set for Streaming Debut on Disney+
a4977d3fa4:d8d73dfdeaea39bb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d8d73dfdeaea39bb.summary: Summary Marvel Studios and Disney+ will officially begin streaming Avengers Endgame: Encore on Friday November 13The extended cut includes four new scenes connecting to Avengers: Doomsday and propelled the film to 2.925 billion USD at the global box officeThe release precedes the December debut of Doomsday and the rollout of Disney's new Infinity Vision premium theater format Marvel Studios and streaming platform Disney+ have officially set the streaming release date for Avengers Endgame: Encore, bringing the extended cut to audiences on Friday, November 13, 2026. Scheduled to arrive roughly one month before Avengers: Doomsday debuts in theaters on December 18, the expanded release incorporates four brand-new scenes that directly tie into the storyline of the upcoming ensemble film.During its theatrical re-release, Avengers Endgame: Encore made a powerful box office statement, opening to $26 million USD domestically and $86 million USD globally. That commercial performance pushed Endgame past Avatar to reclaim the title of the highest-grossing film of all time with a historic $2.925 billion USD. a4977d3fa4:645e2a59d11e97b1.summary: Summary Ulysse Nardin marks 25 years of the Freak with the 50-piece Freak [S Purple Enamel].The timepiece spotlights a rotating purple guilloché-flinqué enamel hour disc crafted by Donzé Cadrans.Priced at $174,400 USD, the timepiece is driven by the dual-oscillator Calibre UN-251 with 72 hours of power reserve. Ulysse Nardin is marking two milestones in 2026: 180 years since its founding in Le Locle and 25 years since the debut of the Freak. Launched in 2001 and designed by Dr. Ludwig Oechslin, the original Freak broke every convention with no dial, no hands and no crown and a movement that rotated to tell the time, while also being the first watch to use silicon components.The latest chapter is the Freak [S Purple Enamel], the final titanium Freak [S] with an enamel hour disc. Two oversized silicon balance wheels, each tilted at 20 degrees and fitted with DIAMonSIL escapements, are linked by a 47-part vertical differential on ceramic ball bearings, which the brand calls the smallest of its kind in the world, averaging their rates for greater accuracy. The mechanism spreads across six gear planes instead of the usual two, and about 95% of its parts are in motion at any time. The patented Grinder winding system keeps everything running for 72 hours.True to the Freak's rules, the wearer sets the time by unlocking a latch at 6 o'clock and turning the bezel, and winds it by flipping the watch over and turning the caseback. Each piece is assembled start to finish by a single Grandes Complications watchmaker. The purple hour disc is the edition's standout feature. It was made in-house at Donzé Cadrans, the Swiss enamel workshop that Ulysse Nardin acquired in 2011. Unlike a static dial, this disc rotates as part of the movement, so it is built on an 18-carat white gold base chosen for its stability under repeated kiln firings. a4977d3fa4:7dd4915887a4ca27.summary: Summary Angie Martinez is releasing never-before-heard portions of a Tupac Shakur interview she recorded at his Los Angeles home months before his deathThe four-episode video podcast pairs the original audio with reflections from 15 guests who lived through the era or helped shape how it’s rememberedMartinez withheld the most inflammatory parts for nearly three decades out of concern they could inflame an already dangerous climate Netflix is set to premiere The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez, a four-episode video podcast built around previously unreleased material from Martinez’s 1996 sit-down with Tupac Shakur. The Radio Hall of Famer and New York Times bestselling author recorded the conversation early in her New York radio career, aired only select portions at the time and kept the rest private for close to 30 years.The interview itself came together through an unlikely detour. Tupac first contacted Martinez hoping she would appear in his “I Ain’t Mad at Cha” music video, a request she turned down given the tension surrounding him in New York at the time. Their conversation shifted when he made clear his grievances weren’t aimed at the entire city, a point Martinez felt the public needed to hear directly from him, so he invited her to Los Angeles to record at his home, where he greeted her with New York pizza to make her feel welcome.Back at the station, Martinez made the editorial call that defines the series. She broadcast the sections that conveyed Tupac’s core message that he wasn’t feuding with a whole coast, then physically sliced out the more volatile remarks with a razor blade, worried they could hurt people, fracture relationships or escalate an already deadly situation. His death months later only complicated the choice further, as she felt responsible for protecting words that were never intended to be his last public statement. a4977d3fa4:f9298d6e50c7d865.summary: Summary Kendrick Lamar’s “The Blacker the Berry” soundtracks a gunfight in an episode of the new Netflix anime Bass X Machina Brian Tyree Henry stars as Bass Reeves, whose mid-reload warning to his enemies kicks off the trackThe song arrives as a remix reworked to blend into the episode’s sound design Netflix’s Bass X Machina has pulled Kendrick Lamar’s “The Blacker the Berry” into one of its fiercest set pieces, a close-quarters gunfight staged inside a moving train. The 2015 To Pimp a Butterfly remix track arrives at the exact moment the scene tips from tense standoff into full-blown firefight, turning a Netflix action beat into a Kendrick moment.Everything hinges on a single line from Brian Tyree Henry’s Bass Reeves. Surrounded and outgunned, the lawman calmly tells his attackers they have only as long as it takes him to load his weapon to change their minds, and when nobody takes the offer, Kendrick’s opening bars hit. The version heard on screen isn’t a straight needle drop either, as the song has been reshaped to mesh with the episode’s gunshots, rattling train cars and score.The pairing carries extra weight given who the show is built around. The real Bass Reeves, born into slavery, became one of the first Black deputy US marshals west of the Mississippi River and is often cited as a possible inspiration for the Lone Ranger. a4977d3fa4:748062df733fe33d.summary: Summary The Audi Nuvolari will carry a $700,000 USD price tag, with exactly 182 units allocated for the United StatesPacking a 987-horsepower hybrid V-8 powertrain, the brand's fastest production car clocks a 2.5-second sprint to 60 mphDeliveries for the highly customizable supercar will officially commence in the first half of 2028 Three years after the end of the R8, the Audi Nuvolari steps into the spotlight, signaling a pivot in the German marque’s high-performance lineup. That output propels the supercar to 60 mph in a claimed 2.5 seconds, on its way to a top speed of 217 mph.Visually, the machine departs from its predecessors with a brutalist design. Audi unveiled the vehicle in June in a matte gray finish, but future owners will access an extensive bespoke catalog. The customization options include over 50 gloss paint colors, 10 matte paint colors and an option to leave the carbon-fiber bodywork fully exposed. Buyers can also select from 13 different brake caliper colors.Deliveries of the Audi Nuvolari will commence in the United States in the first half of 2028. a4977d3fa4:6e32a337e86f7726.title: Kurono Tokyo’s “Structure” Chronograph S1 Is Hajime Asaoka’s Take on the Perfect Tool Watch
a4977d3fa4:6e32a337e86f7726.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6e32a337e86f7726.summary: Summary Hajime Asaoka launches Kurono Tokyo’s STRUCTURE series with the 40mm “Structure” Chronograph S1.A four-layer dial nearly eliminates parallax between the chronograph hand and indices.Available in Teal, Salmon, and White, it drops November 19 with a price tag of $3,690 USD. Kurono Tokyo is launching a new design direction. The "Structure" Chronograph S1 is the first release in the STRUCTURE series, which founder and acclaimed independent watchmaker Hajime Asaoka describes as a new kind of tool watch. Earlier Kurono pieces were built on classical watchmaking proportions with a modern edge, but the S1 puts function first. It packs a full tool-watch chronograph into a 40mm case, slightly larger than the brand's usual sizing. "My design ethos for this project can be distilled into two words: Functional Elegance," Asaoka said in the release.The heart of the watch is its four-layer dial, built to bring each hand as close as possible to the markers it reads against. The result is that the central chronograph hand sits with almost no parallax over the indices, making elapsed-time readings more precise. The subdials are enlarged as far as the layout allows, and their counter hands share the same fluorescent orange as the chronograph hand for quick reading at a glance.The S1 comes in Teal, Salmon and White, each in a high-polished 316L stainless steel case that is 13.15mm thick including its sapphire box crystal, 50.2mm lug-to-lug, with 22mm lugs and a rubber strap. Inside is the automatic NE86PWT movement, beating at 28,800 vph with 34 jewels and roughly 45 hours of power reserve.The S1 is priced at $3,690 USD and will be sold exclusively online through Kurono Tokyo's website starting November 19, 2026, at 11 p.m. JST/ 9 a.m. in New York. The release is limited and won't be repeated, with deliveries expected from mid-December 2026. d006da4fe3:cccd877b2427dfd1.author: Charles Kupchan
d006da4fe3:cccd877b2427dfd1.summary: In just a few days’ time, U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin could be holding a three-way summit on the sidelines of next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen, China. According to The Wall Street Journal, Putin floated the idea of a trialogue last month as an opportunity to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. No firm plan has yet been announced, but even the prospect of this meeting has provoked widespread consternation. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski warned against a repeat of the Yalta Conference of 1945, when U.S. President Franklin Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill capitulated to Soviet leader Joseph Stalin’s push for the Soviet Union to dominate Eastern Europe. U.S. Senator Chris Coons wrote on X that “There can be no talks about Ukraine’s future without Ukraine at the table, and there can be no real negotiations as long as Trump signals weakness and servitude to Xi and Putin at every opportunity.”

d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.title: America’s AI Ambitions Depend on Taiwan
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.author: Lin Chia-lung
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.summary: The United States and China are locked in a global competition to determine who will dominate artificial intelligence and whether it will be democracies or autocracies that set the standards and values of the new digital age. The United States leads the world in the sophistication and power of its artificial intelligence models, and its innovation base and investment in research and development remain unparalleled.But AI competition is much broader than modeling alone. It encompasses a technology ecosystem that includes power generation, servers, and deployment in real-world applications. Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, has described the AI industry as a five-layer cake with energy at its base and chips, infrastructure, models, and applications above it. To win the AI race with China, the United States needs to maintain or establish an advantage in each of these layers. And to do that, the United States needs Taiwan.

d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.title: The New Energy Stalemate in Ukraine
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.author: Tatiana Mitrova, Sergey Vakulenko
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.summary: Tatiana Mitrova, a fellow at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy and former energy scholar at Moscow’s Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Vakulenko, an oil and gas expert at Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center, argue that Russia and Ukraine are locked in an energy war that has become an adaptation spiral, despite growing human and economic costs and despite current US pressure on Ukraine. They observe Ukraine’s remarkable ability to withstand Russian strikes, while questioning claims that long-range Ukrainian strikes will be able to achieve game-changing damage on Russia. Ukraine and Russia have transformed the role of energy warfare in modern conflict, drawing on low costs drones but also new forms of technological resilience that are likely to make wars longer and more dangerous.

d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.title: A Less-Is-More Strategy for America

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.title: How Russia Sees the World Now

d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.title: AI Is a Choice
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.author: Alex Imas, Mohamed A. El-Erian, James Manyika
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.summary: Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, and James Manyika, leading voices at the intersection of business and technology, argue that realizing AI’s potential requires giving workers, communities, AI labs, infrastructure developers, and big companies a share of the gains. Using insights from game theory, they argue that increased cooperation can make AI work for all.

d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.title: Empires of AI
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.author: Niall Ferguson, Lisa Klaassen, Eric Schmidt
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.summary: In this essay, Niall Ferguson, one of the world’s foremost experts on imperial history, teams up the former CEO of Google, Eric Schmidt, and the researcher Lisa Klaasen to make the provocative argument that AI is an inherently “imperial technology”—and to reveal what the fate of past empires might say about the future of U.S.-Chinese competition in a world shaped by AI.

d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.title: “Earth Satellites and Foreign Policy”
d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.summary: The advent of a new technology invariably comes with strategic implications, raising the question of who will benefit and whether risks can be managed. In 1957, following the Soviet Sputnik launch, U.S. policymakers and analysts recognized that the satellite, as the American physicist and engineer Lloyd Berkner observed in these pages, would bring transformative effects. The United States could not risk losing out, Berkner argued, but nor should governments allow geopolitical tensions to prevent the technology’s broad benefits from emerging.

d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.title: Europe’s Credibility Gap

d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.summary: Ngaire Woods, Dean of Oxford’s Blavatnik School of Government, Claas Mertens, also at Oxford, have written a piece arguing that Europe, despite its attempts at self-sufficiency, remains dependent on an unpredictable United States. The continent needs to address this vulnerability so that it can convince other countries, many of which find themselves similarly vulnerable to great-power coercion, that it is a worthy partner.

d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War

d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.summary: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.

d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO

fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.title: Intangible Capital as a Source of Economic Growth and Productivity: A Literature Review and Policy Guidelines
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.author: Rouvinen, Petri
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.summary: Abstract This review synthesizes the latest scholarly evidence on intangible capital. Drawing on 60 recent studies across macro, meso, and micro levels (anchored by firm-level data from Finland, broader Europe, the US, and Asia) it demonstrates that intangible investments have emerged as the preeminent engine of economic growth, competitiveness, and productivity. The literature yields three critical imperatives for public policy. First, the measurement and statistical tracking of intangibles require a fundamental overhaul; at present, a swath of these investments remains invisible in official data and absent from corporate balance sheets. Second, policymakers must broaden their horizons beyond narrow research and development (R&D) subsidies. Modern innovation policy must embrace the full spectrum of intangible assets – spanning software, data, organizational capital, management capabilities, and brand equity –, while capitalizing on the vital synergies between them. Third, the scalable nature of intangible capital demands a synchronized approach to competition policy, innovation strategy, and corporate finance. Authorities must strike a delicate balance: cultivating the incentives and finance necessary to fuel intangible investments, while simultaneously preventing harmful market concentration and fostering broad diffusion of knowledge.

fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.title: Economists, Economic Knowledge, and Central Banks
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.author: Juan Acosta
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.summary: What do economists do in central banks? Why do central banks hire economists? This book investigates the evolving role of economists and economic knowledge within central banks, arguing that their current centrality is neither self-evident nor historically inevitable. While the presence and influence of economists in central banks today may seem natural, this book shows that it is the result of a complex, gradual, and uneven historical process shaped by institutional structures, disciplinary transformations, and shifting relationships between science and policy. Drawing on a rich but dispersed body of literature, the book traces how economists progressively gained authority through the establishment of statistics departments, the adoption of macroeconometric models, and the emergence of a shared cognitive infrastructure between academia and central banks. Rather than focusing on individuals or doctrines, it examines general trends and institutional shifts across a series of national case studies to show how central banks function as boundary organizations, at the intersection of policy and science.

fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.title: Known Unknowns: Knowledge, Confidence, and Public Opinion on Water Reuse
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.author: Marco Dâ€™Errico
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.summary: Public acceptance can constrain treated-wastewater reuse, but less is known about whether citizens provide a substantive view at all. An influential account of opposition to contested technologies predicts that the strongest opponents know the least while believing they know the most. We test that joint prediction using a knowledgeâ€“attitudesâ€“practices survey of 1, 069 households in Barbados. The survey separately measures demonstrated topic knowledge, self-assessed knowledge, willingness to use reclaimed water, and explicit 'donâ€™t know' responses. Among respondents who provide a complete willingness profile, demonstrated knowledge is essentially unrelated to acceptance, whereas self-assessed knowledge is positively associated with acceptance. The predicted knowledge-overconfidence configuration therefore does not appear in this setting. The strongest knowledge gradient instead lies on the response margin: a one-standard-deviation increase in demonstrated knowledge is associated with a 5.8-percentage-point lower probability of giving at least one 'donâ€™t know' response, against a base rate of 22.6 per cent. The relationship reappears in three sectoral attitude batteries and attenuates by about 19 per cent after controlling for out-of-module nonresponse. The evidence therefore points away from confidently mistaken opposition and toward a sizeable group that is less knowledgeable and more likely to express uncertainty.

fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.title: Venture Capital and Customer Capital
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.author: Amir Sufi
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.summary: Venture capital specializes in the financing of customer capital intensive firms—firms with higher sales and marketing expense to revenue ratios, a higher wage bill for sales and marketing employees, and a higher tendency to apply for trademarks—and they do so more than other financial intermediaries. Venture capitalists target high customer capital industries with low knowledge capital but avoid high knowledge capital industries that lack customer capital. Firms tilt investment toward customer capital leading up to the initial venture capital investment, after which their scale accelerates rapidly. Venture capitalists focus on financing customer capital because such investments require tolerance for substantial risks of failure in pursuit of extreme upside potential, as characterized by power law returns. This return profile fits customer capital investments more closely than investments in knowledge capital. Venture capitalists that sprinkle small investments across a large number of firms, colloquially referred to as the “spray and pray” strategy, target customer capital industries for investment, whereas venture capitalists that commit larger amounts to a small number of firms target knowledge capital industries. The venture capital focus on customer capital reflects a shift away from its traditional focus on knowledge capital intensive firms over the past 30 years.

fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.title: From Balanced Growth to Innovation Cycles: A Solow-Type Semi-Endogenous Growth Model
fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.author: Thi Kim Cuong Pham
fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.summary: We develop a growth model with an R&D sector in which the elasticity of innovation with respect to existing knowledge can be negative. We investigate the existence and uniqueness of a balanced growth path (BGP) and derive closed-form growth factors, showing that productivity and output growth are semi-endogenous and population-driven. We also establish the global stability under a general production function. Under testable parameter restrictions, the economy converges to the BGP. However, when the knowledge elasticity is sufficiently low, a Jacobian-based condition implies instability, and an N-period innovation cycle can emerge. Comparative statics are conducted to explore the impact of several factors, including research efficiency, input elasticity, and population growth. Numerical simulations map out transitions and mark the points at which stability is lost. They make clear when innovation frictions endanger balanced growth and provide practical guidance for R&D and demographic policy.
